## Tours through Puerto Río Tranquilo: Marble Caves and San Rafael Glacier

[Puerto Río Tranquilo](/chile/place/puerto-rio-tranquilo/) is a village beside [Lake General Carrera](/chile/place/general-carrera-lake/) in the Aysén Region. From here, travelers set off for the [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) and follow the road through [Exploradores Valley](/chile/place/exploradores-valley/) to boat routes near [San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/).

When choosing a tour, what matters most is **not the total number of days spent across South America, but how many nights and excursions are devoted specifically to Aysén**. Ada Tours offers a short trip based in the village, a wider itinerary within Chile and a journey combining Chile with Bolivia.

## Three ways to travel through the village

**[Marble Caves and San Rafael Glacier: 3 Days](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/)** is a short private tour of Aysén. Day one includes a transfer from Balmaceda Airport along the [Carretera Austral](/chile/place/carretera-austral/) and accommodation in Puerto Río Tranquilo. The next day is devoted to traveling via Exploradores and taking a boat to San Rafael; on another day, travelers visit the Marble Caves. Both nights are spent in the village. This option lets you focus on the region's two principal experiences on the water.

**[Hidden Treasures of Chile: 9 Days](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/)** adds Santiago, the Atacama Desert and Torres del Paine to Aysén. The itinerary includes a journey along the Carretera Austral, a night in Puerto Río Tranquilo, a boat excursion to San Rafael and a separate outing to the Marble Caves. It provides greater contrasts in natural scenery, although flights and transfers between distant regions take considerable time.

**[Hidden Treasures of Bolivia and Chile: 16 Days](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/)** combines the Uyuni Salt Flat and Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons with the Atacama, southern Patagonia and central Chile. Puerto Río Tranquilo forms part of the longer journey, together with San Rafael and the Marble Caves. Choose this option if you want to explore two countries and are comfortable with a more demanding schedule.

| Itinerary | Best suited to |
|---|---|
| 3 days in Aysén | Two principal boat excursions |
| 9 days in Chile | Atacama, Aysén and Patagonia |
| 16 days: Bolivia + Chile | Multiple countries and natural regions |

## The Marble Caves and San Rafael are different excursions

The [Marble Caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) are on Lake General Carrera. A small boat can approach the arches and rock walls carved by water into the marble. The colors of the lake and reflections are particularly impressive in favorable weather, but going out on the water depends on wind and waves. This excursion focuses on the rocky shoreline and lake landscape.

[San Rafael Glacier](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) requires a different type of journey. The road through [Exploradores Valley](/chile/place/exploradores-valley/) leads to the departure point for a boat passage to the glacier, where you may see icebergs and the glacier's ice front. A full day is devoted to this outing. Its timing and navigability depend on the weather and the individual operator's conditions.

On the short 3-day itinerary, both excursions form the core of the trip. On multi-region journeys, they fit between flights and overland transfers. When choosing, compare the order of days and time buffers: replacing one excursion with the other would change the substance of the trip.

## Getting to Puerto Río Tranquilo

On Ada Tours itineraries, Balmaceda is the starting point for the Aysén section. The road then follows the [Carretera Austral](/chile/place/carretera-austral/) towards Lake General Carrera. This is a long drive through sparsely populated areas, so it makes sense to combine it with an overnight stay instead of scheduling both boat excursions on your arrival day.

Aysén's terrain and weather differ from the Atacama: rain, cold winds and rapidly changing clouds are possible. Waterproof outerwear, protection for your camera, shoes with good grip and a warm extra layer are useful for boat outings. On gravel sections of road, consider the surface conditions and travel time.

The 9-day itinerary returns to Balmaceda after visiting the Marble Caves, then continues south towards Puerto Natales. Therefore, [tours via Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/tour/) should be seen as a continuation of a wider journey through Chile, not as a nearby excursion from Puerto Río Tranquilo.

## Choosing the right duration

If your main goals are the lake and glacier, the [3-day trip](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) involves fewer additional transport stages. For a first visit to Chile covering several contrasting regions, the [9-day itinerary](/chile/tour/chile-hidden-secrets-9-days/) is a natural choice. To combine Patagonia with high-altitude Bolivia, consider the [16-day program](/multi-country/tour/bolivia-chile-hidden-treasures-16-days/).

Before booking, ask how many nights are spent in Puerto Río Tranquilo, what type of boat is used, what happens if weather forces an excursion to change, how long the overland transfers take and which services are included at your selected rate. You can compare other routes in our [Chile tours catalog](/chile/tour/), although not all visit Aysén.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Puerto Río Tranquilo

### Can you see the Marble Caves and San Rafael on one trip?

Yes. Both sites are included in the [private 3-day itinerary](/chile/tour/marble-caves-san-rafael-3-days/) and in longer programs. The glacier has a separate day, while the caves are visited on their own boat excursion.

### Is it worth staying overnight?

For an itinerary with both boat outings, overnight stays make the logistics much easier. The short tour includes 2 nights in Puerto Río Tranquilo, separating the drive from the excursions.

### Does a Marble Caves excursion replace the glacier trip?

No. The [caves](/chile/place/marble-caves/) are rock arches on the lake, while [San Rafael](/chile/place/san-rafael-glacier/) is a glacier reached by a longer boat journey. The choice depends on your time, interests and the weather.

## Puerto Varas, Chile: what to see and how to plan a visit

Puerto Varas lies in southern [Chile](/chile/), on the shore of the large Lake Llanquihue. In clear weather, the symmetrical snow-covered cone of Osorno Volcano rises above the water. This is often the first memorable sight of the Lake District, a region of wooded hills, volcanic peaks and deep lakes.

The city works both for a short stop and as a base for several days. You can walk along the waterfront, look at the architecture of the central streets and venture out to surrounding natural attractions. However, these activities require different amounts of time: **Puerto Varas, Lake Llanquihue and Osorno Volcano are three related but distinct stops**.

## What to see in Puerto Varas itself

Start with the Lake Llanquihue waterfront. It offers broad views of the water and volcanoes, and a relaxed walk helps you understand the city's layout. Because the weather changes quickly, the panorama can look quite different from one moment to another: sometimes the summit of Osorno is clearly visible, while at other times clouds conceal it.

Puerto Varas' architecture reflects the region's German settler heritage. Buildings with characteristic timber details, steep roofs and European influences remain along the streets. This cultural background is also apparent in local cuisine, baked goods and the traditions of small family-run businesses. For a first visit, allowing time for a walk is more rewarding than stopping for just one volcano photograph.

The city's cafes and restaurants are particularly welcome after a nature excursion. The Lake District is a place to try local dishes; when choosing a restaurant with lake views, consider the weather. An outdoor terrace is less comfortable in rain, while windows facing the water and mountains can still create a memorable setting.

## Lake Llanquihue: views and excursions

[Lake Llanquihue](/chile/place/llanquihue-lake/) is the area's central natural feature. Towns and villages around its shores include Puerto Varas, Frutillar and Puerto Octay. Their waterfronts and landscapes differ, so traveling around the lake reveals several distinct parts of the Lake District rather than a single viewpoint.

Chile's national tourism portal describes a circular route along the shoreline measuring approximately 186 km. This is a guide for a substantial road trip, not a short walk. Depending on your stops, you can combine volcano views with local culture and gastronomy.

Kayaking, cycling and other water-based activities depend on the season, weather, equipment and specific provider. Arrange them separately if they are important to your journey.

## Osorno Volcano and the national park

[Osorno Volcano](/chile/place/osorno-volcano/) rises above the eastern part of Llanquihue and is one of Chile's most recognizable natural landmarks. Roads from the Ensenada area lead towards its slopes. This is a separate trip from the city, not an attraction located on the waterfront.

You can combine views of Osorno with a visit to Vicente Pérez Rosales National Park. This protected area has several sectors, roads and trails. Visiting specific parts requires up-to-date information on permits, weather and access.

**Current restriction:** CONAF reports that the Petrohué Falls sector has been closed since September 30, 2026, for infrastructure maintenance until further notice. The presence of the falls in an older itinerary does not mean they are accessible today. Check which areas are open on CONAF's official website before booking, and agree on a permitted alternative.

## How many days to allow for Puerto Varas

| Time available | Suggested plan |
|---|---|
| A few hours | Waterfront and city center |
| One day | City and lakeside views |
| 2–3 days | Lake, volcano and nearby villages |
| Longer stay | Explore the Lake District in depth |

The ideal duration depends on whether you simply want to admire the volcano from shore or visit natural attractions nearby. For several longer excursions, avoid packing too many destinations into one day: driving and changeable weather require extra time.

Puerto Varas is convenient to visit after arriving in Puerto Montt. The nearest major airport, El Tepual (PMC), serves the region. An overland transfer is then required; its duration depends on road conditions and the location of your accommodation.

Rain is possible in southern Chile in different seasons, so a waterproof jacket, comfortable shoes and an extra layer are useful even when daytime temperatures feel pleasant.

## Puerto Varas on Ada Tours itineraries

Our current [33-day South America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-luxury-33-days/) includes Puerto Varas as part of an exploration of southern Chile, the lake and volcanoes. This reflects the city's role as a base for regional excursions. Specific stops and activities, including the Petrohué Falls, should be checked against current park restrictions and the actual tour description.

If nature is your main interest, compare our [nature and wildlife destinations](/interests/wildlife/) with the southern Chile itinerary. On a first trip, several days in the Lake District are often more practical than trying to cover every natural attraction in one excursion.

## Frequently asked questions about Puerto Varas

### What should you see first: the city, lake or Osorno?

If time is short, begin on the Puerto Varas waterfront, where you can see Lake Llanquihue and, in favorable weather, Osorno Volcano. Reaching the volcano's slopes or other sections of the lake requires a separate trip.

### Can you reach Puerto Varas via Puerto Montt?

Yes. Puerto Montt is a major transport hub for the region, and El Tepual Airport handles flights. Ground transfers to Puerto Varas are available.

### Are the Petrohué Falls currently open?

According to CONAF's published notice, the falls sector has been closed for maintenance since September 30, 2026, until further notice. Check the current status of this specific part of the park before visiting; other sectors have their own access rules.

## Puerto Williams: a town on the Beagle Channel on Navarino Island

Puerto Williams lies on the northern shore of Navarino Island in the Chilean part of the Tierra del Fuego archipelago. The Beagle Channel passes in front of the town, while forested slopes and the rocky summits of the Dientes de Navarino mountains rise beyond its houses and piers. It is one of the southernmost towns on the planet and a starting point for exploring the subantarctic landscapes of [Chile](/chile/).

Two very different worlds meet here. Fishing boats and yachts lie along the waterfront, quiet town life continues a few blocks from the harbor, and beyond the built-up area are trails where weather and trail conditions matter more than the distance shown on a map. Puerto Williams is therefore worth considering both as a destination in its own right and as a short stop on a sea expedition.

## Where Puerto Williams is and how it differs from Ushuaia

Puerto Williams stands on Navarino Island, south of the main island of Tierra del Fuego. Across the Beagle Channel on the Argentine side lies the Ushuaia area. The two places often feature in the same journey through the archipelago, but they belong to different countries: ordinary border and immigration rules apply when traveling between them.

Both settlements are sometimes described as the "southernmost city" in tourism materials. For practical planning, their geography matters more: Puerto Williams sits on Navarino on the southern shore of the Beagle Channel and provides access to Chilean sea routes. Ushuaia is on the Argentine side and has different transport infrastructure.

The town is part of the Cabo de Hornos commune, which also includes [Cape Horn](/chile/place/cape-horn/). However, Cape Horn cannot be reached by an ordinary walk from the town waterfront: it requires a separate sea voyage, dependent on the vessel and weather.

## What to see in Puerto Williams

### Waterfront, harbor and channel panorama

The easiest introduction to the town begins at the water. In clear conditions, you can see the opposite shore of the channel and mountain slopes. Fishing boats, small piers and low buildings show how the settlement has adapted to life in this remote southern region.

For a short stop, it is better to leave time for a walk along accessible sections of the waterfront than to try to fit in a distant mountain route. Winds can strengthen quickly, so even a town walk calls for warm layers and a windproof jacket.

### Yaghan culture

The archipelago's history began long before modern ports appeared. For generations, the Indigenous Yaghan people lived among the channels and islands, traveling by water and relying on marine resources. In Puerto Williams, the Martín Gusinde Anthropological Museum (Museo Antropológico Martín Gusinde) is dedicated to this heritage.

The museum connects the names of channels and islands familiar from cruises with the lives of the people who inhabited them. Plan a museum visit separately: a ship calling at the port does not itself mean that an excursion to the museum is included.

### The natural environment of Navarino Island

Forests, wet areas and mountain trails begin beyond the town. Omora Park introduces visitors to local ecosystems, including mosses, lichens and other plants of the cool south. Visits are organized according to the access rules in force.

Walks of different lengths let you discover the island beyond the seascapes. When choosing a route, consider wind, rain, ground conditions and daylight hours. Even during the warmer season, hiking conditions can differ greatly from the weather on the town waterfront.

## Dientes de Navarino: a trek for experienced travelers

The Dientes de Navarino mountains are known for a demanding multi-day trekking circuit. According to Chile's national tourism portal, completing the full loop usually takes **4–5 days**. The trail crosses mountain passes, rocky slopes, boggy ground and exposed high terrain.

Such a hike requires separate preparation, reliable waterproof clothing, navigation skills and an assessment of physical demands. It is a standalone adventure, not an extension of an hour-long tour of Puerto Williams. Check current trail registration requirements and recommendations from local authorities when planning.

If mountains are your main motivation, begin with [adventure tours](/interests/adventure/) and compare the available time and difficulty. For a short stay on the island, a coastal walk or easy trail with conditions that can be checked locally is a more realistic choice.

## Getting there and how much time to allow

The principal routes to Puerto Williams connect with [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/): air services and ferry passages. Check the current schedule, journey duration and availability before booking. Wind and other weather conditions in southern Chile can affect departure times for both flights and vessels.

The time needed depends on your aim:

| Type of visit | Time to allow |
|---|---|
| Cruise stop | According to the ship's schedule |
| Town and surroundings | 1–2 days |
| Mountain trekking circuit | 4–5 days plus a buffer |

These are planning guidelines, not the duration of an included Ada Tours excursion. Extra time is particularly useful when connecting with a flight or another ship: weather in the archipelago is unpredictable.

## Puerto Williams on routes to Cape Horn and Antarctica

On our current [6-day Antarctica Express journey](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/), the route starts in Ushuaia. The ship enters the Beagle Channel and heads towards Puerto Williams before continuing to [Cape Horn](/chile/place/cape-horn/). The later stages explore Antarctic regions. The full multi-day trek across Navarino is not included.

When choosing a trip, distinguish between a route passing through the Puerto Williams area and a guaranteed landing, town excursion or overnight stay. These are confirmed only by the specific tour description and the vessel's actual plan. If you are more interested in visiting Chile by land, compare separate [Chile itineraries](/chile/tour/) with sea expeditions.

## When to visit and what to pack

The Southern Hemisphere summer runs from December through February. Longer daylight hours make it convenient for coastal observation and walking. Yet wind and precipitation can make conditions feel colder even in summer. Hiking conditions may be more difficult at other times of year.

For a sea journey, take a windproof jacket, warm mid-layer, shoes with nonslip soles, a hat and rain protection. Mountain trekking calls for an entirely different equipment list and a separate safety plan. Pack for the type of journey, not merely for the region's name on the map.

## Frequently asked questions about Puerto Williams

### Is Puerto Williams in Chile or Argentina?

It is in Chile, on Navarino Island. The Argentine Ushuaia area is across the Beagle Channel.

### Can you see Cape Horn from town?

Puerto Williams serves as a departure point for sea routes to [Cape Horn](/chile/place/cape-horn/), but the cape itself is far from the town's waterfront. Visiting it requires a separate voyage.

### Are a few hours enough to see the town?

A few hours may be enough for a waterfront stroll. The museum, nature trails and especially the full Dientes de Navarino trek require additional time and an agreed itinerary.

### Is the Dientes de Navarino trek included in an Antarctic cruise?

It is normally a separate multi-day journey. It is not listed on our published [Antarctica Express](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/) itinerary, so it should not be assumed to be included.

## Which tours visit Puerto Williams in Chile?

[Puerto Williams](/chile/place/puerto-williams/) stands on Navarino Island beside the Beagle Channel. For sea travelers, it is an important landmark on the route from Tierra del Fuego towards [Cape Horn](/chile/place/cape-horn/). However, seeing the town on a cruise itinerary does not guarantee a separate excursion through its streets or a multi-day stay on the island.

Ada Tours' current selection includes [Antarctica Express: Ushuaia, Cape Horn and Antarctica in 6 Days](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/), which passes through Puerto Williams. This is an expedition with an outward sea voyage followed by a return by air. The town is part of the Chilean section of the route, while the journey's principal days focus on Cape Horn, the Drake Passage and Antarctica.

## How the 6-day expedition works

The journey begins in Ushuaia, where the ship enters the Beagle Channel and heads towards Puerto Williams. It then continues to Cape Horn and crosses the Drake Passage. During the Antarctic stages, the program includes sailing among glaciers and icebergs, landings in Zodiac boats and observing marine wildlife, according to actual conditions on the voyage. The journey ends with a flight from King George Island to [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/).

An important feature is that **the return crossing of the Drake Passage is not made by ship**. Travelers fly back instead. Flights from Antarctica are also weather-dependent, so allow extra time when arranging international connections.

The route includes an introduction to the surroundings of Puerto Williams. However, a guaranteed separate guided walk through town, museum visit or mountain trek on Navarino is not listed as an independently included service. If visiting a particular place ashore is essential, confirm the landing arrangements for your chosen departure.

## Expedition cruise versus a separate visit to Navarino

| Format | Main purpose |
|---|---|
| Expedition cruise | Beagle Channel, Cape Horn, Antarctica |
| Island stay | Town, museums, local trails |
| Mountain trek | Dientes de Navarino |

An independent visit to Puerto Williams offers a chance to explore Yaghan heritage, visit the Martín Gusinde Museum and choose a walk on the island. Trekking in the Dientes de Navarino mountains is far more demanding than a typical coastal excursion: it requires time, physical preparation and specialist equipment. **The 6-day Antarctic cruise does not automatically include this hike.**

Another distinction is the departure point. For a separate visit to Puerto Williams, you may be able to fly from Punta Arenas or travel by sea. The named expedition tour, however, begins **in Ushuaia**, so an extra ticket to Navarino does not replace its embarkation point.

## What affects the schedule and visit conditions?

Southern Chilean waters are known for strong winds and changeable weather. Even in summer, warm layers, a waterproof jacket and shoes with good grip are essential. The sheltered waters of the Beagle Channel and the exposed Drake Passage can differ sharply in wave height and how the journey feels on board.

Three things matter most: where travelers embark, whether a landing at Puerto Williams is possible, and how much time remains between the return from Antarctica and the next flight. We help coordinate these stages and check documents for the specific nationality and travel dates. The precise expedition conditions come from the selected itinerary, not from general descriptions of the town.

To compare options, see [cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/), [multi-country journeys](/multi-country/) and [Chile tours](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about journeys through Puerto Williams

### Can you go ashore in Puerto Williams?

The 6-day expedition description mentions exploring the surroundings, but a separate guaranteed landing is not specified. Confirm it for your particular sailing.

### Where does the tour featuring Puerto Williams begin?

In Ushuaia, on the Argentine side of Tierra del Fuego. After the sea passage and Antarctica, the program finishes in Punta Arenas.

### Does it include the Dientes de Navarino trek?

No. Mountain trekking requires a separate itinerary, time and preparation.

### What happens if the weather prevents the Antarctic flight?

Departure may be postponed. Allow for weather restrictions and avoid tight connections after Antarctica.

## Puna Pau: the red-stone quarry on Easter Island

**Puna Pau** is an archaeological site on [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/) where reddish volcanic material was quarried to make **pukao**, the stone topknots placed on some moai statues. Large worked stone blocks still lie on the grassy slope. They offer a sense of how Rapa Nui craftspeople prepared parts of these sculptures before transporting them to ceremonial platforms.

Puna Pau answers a question raised by statues with red elements on their heads: where did the material come from? Most of the main stone figures were carved at [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), while the red topknots came from a different quarry. These 2 sites reveal distinct parts of one complex tradition.

## What are pukao and how do they differ from moai?

Pukao are massive carved stone elements placed on the heads of certain moai. They are often called "hats," although their exact symbolism, including possible connections to hairstyles or headwear, remains a matter of scholarly interpretation. The stone statue and its pukao were made separately.

The pukao were carved from **red volcanic scoria**, a relatively porous rock. Its color stands out sharply from the stone used for most statues. Quarrying, shaping and moving such heavy blocks required organized labor.

Rapa Nui National Park notes that material from Puna Pau was also used for certain decorative stone elements. The site therefore tells us about more than the famous red topknots: it also illustrates the islanders' craft technologies.

## What to see at the quarry

### Red cylindrical blocks

Puna Pau's most recognizable feature is the large cylindrical and rounded blocks of red stone scattered among the grass. Some were left at different stages of production. Their size suggests how much work went into making and transporting each topknot.

This is not a row of completed moai: the site's main significance lies in its preserved traces of production. Do not touch the blocks, attempt to move stones or use them as platforms for photographs.

### Volcanic hill and quarry

The quarry is located on a small volcanic hill. According to the national park, many years of stone extraction altered the shape of the local crater. Traces of human activity lie alongside the natural landforms, making Puna Pau interesting from a geological perspective as well.

### Views towards Hanga Roa

Permitted viewpoints offer views towards [Hanga Roa](/chile/place/hanga-roa/), the island's principal settlement. The panorama complements the archaeological visit, but visitors must not leave marked paths to get a better photograph.

## Puna Pau, Rano Raraku and Ahu Akivi: how do they differ?

A sightseeing day often includes several sites connected with moai statues, although each tells a different story.

| Site | What it reveals |
|---|---|
| Puna Pau | Stone pukao |
| [Rano Raraku](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/) | How moai were made |
| [Ahu Akivi](/chile/place/ahu-akivi/) | Statues on a platform |

At Rano Raraku, you can see statues at different stages of carving, some still on the volcanic hillside. Ahu Akivi displays finished figures on a ceremonial platform. Puna Pau reveals where the red stone components came from and how they were produced. Together, the sites explain different stages of Rapa Nui material culture.

Another example of ceremonial space is [Tahai](/chile/place/tahai/) near the ocean. Here, the placement of statues and the site's relationship with a coastal settlement are particularly important.

## Where Puna Pau is and how to enter

According to the national park, Puna Pau lies approximately **7 km from Hanga Roa**. It is visited on driving excursions, usually combined with other archaeological stops.

Puna Pau belongs to the protected Rapa Nui National Park. **An admission ticket and an accredited Ma'u Henua guide are required.** Check current opening hours and ticket conditions before traveling, as access arrangements for historic sites can change.

Stay on permitted paths, do not remove stones and do not touch archaeological objects. Closed-toe shoes, water and protection from sun and wind are useful on the open hill. Learn about the methods of stoneworking from your guide's explanations rather than handling the unfinished blocks.

## Puna Pau on Ada Tours itineraries

On our [Colorful Santiago and Mysterious Easter Island tour](/chile/tour/santiago-easter-island/), the quarry visit is planned alongside Ahu Akivi and Tahai. This gives travelers a coherent picture of installed statues, the material used for their topknots and ceremonial platforms.

We also offer a [10-day Private Tour of Chile and Easter Island](/chile/tour/chile-easter-island-private-tour-10-days/). It includes Rapa Nui's monuments as part of a longer journey through the country. Compare the conditions of the particular day, guiding arrangements and sequence of sites in the current itinerary.

More ways to discover the island's heritage can be found among [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [cultural and historical itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/).

## Frequently asked questions about Puna Pau

### Were the moai statues themselves carved at Puna Pau?

Most moai were made at the Rano Raraku quarry. Puna Pau is known for the extraction of red scoria for pukao and other stone objects.

### Did every statue have a red pukao?

No. Topknots appear on only some moai; differences in decoration can be seen by comparing the island's ceremonial platforms.

### Can you visit without a guide?

Access to national park monuments requires an accredited guide and a ticket. Being able to drive up to the quarry does not remove these requirements.

### Is it worth visiting Puna Pau after Rano Raraku?

Yes. Rano Raraku shows how the statues themselves were carved, while Puna Pau reveals the production of the red topknots. Their stories complement each other.
